Trap Space Often found in a patch of a dozen individual 
flowers, the flowers spread over a 5 ft. Square.
Countering These small yellow clusters of flowers rise from the 
green leafed bushes. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 8. Success: 
The Natural Trap is identified.
These pungent, yet beautiful flowers can be found dotted 
across grassy hills and prairies throughout Sol’Kesh. Their 
delicate stems are susceptible to damage from grazing herds 
and have developed a means to keep large fauna at bay as the 
pollen kicked up from disturbing them can induce a rapid 
acting fever. Forcing the lumbering beasts to slow down and 
keep away from the yellow flowers.

Trap Space This gray mold spreads across the bones of long 
dead creatures, its Trap Space filling the same area of the slain 
creature’s size, ranging from Small to Gargantuan.
Countering Usually only the tall thin leaves are visible above 
the soil. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 12. Success: The Natural 
Trap is identified.
Countering While the grass can be seen nearly all year long, it is 
only during the dry fall seasons that it grows silver fibers that can 
spark flame. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 10. Success: The Natural 
Trap is identified
Countering While often hard to see, gray motes of spores 
gently rise off the fuzzy mold that clings to the bones. Wisdom 
(Perception) Check: DC 16. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Often found above extensive Umbrawells caverns, the large 
plant that grows in the loamy soil converts much of the excess 
sulfur dioxide that leaks up from the subterranean acidic 
lifeforms. Stored within chambers within its cloves they will 
loudly expel from seams once disturbed. 
During the fall dry season, when the grasses grow brown and 
brittle, silvery filaments fray at the edges of the flint reed grasses 
which will rub against each other in the heavy winds, sparking 
flame and igniting wide swathes of fields. Seeds are then dropped 
into the smoldering, ash-fertile soil for next year's   growth.
Minuscule spores float across the windswept Farplains, 
harmless in their minute size. Only an infinitesimally rare few 
will chance upon the corpse of a creature to settle on and rapidly 
infest. This slime mold spreads across the bones, rendering the 
beast's corpse into a decrepit version of its living form, covered 
in fruiting bodies ready to propegate.

Alerting Shrill Trigger: When a creature enters its Trap Space. 
Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, the creature that 
triggered the Trap. Failure: The disturbed root releases a highly 
pressurized gas that emits an audible whine that can be clearly 
heard within 300 ft. of it. The shrillion continues to whine until 
the disturbance moves out of its Trap Space.
Cleansing Spark Trigger: When a creature steps within its Trap 
Space. Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 17, the creature that 
triggered the Trap. Failure: A 10 ft. cube of fire engulfs the dry 
grass. An inferno damages any creatures or objects, dealing 11 
(4d10) Fire damage immediately and again every minute. The fire 
can be doused with 10 gallons of water, and within 4 minutes the 
fire burns itself out, leaving behind charred blackened grass.
Gray Lung Trigger: When a creature enters its Trap Space. 
Response - Constitution Saving Throw: DC 16, the creature that 
breathes triggered the Trap. Failure: 7 (3d4) Necrotic damage 
at the start of each of its turns due to the mold invading and 
digesting its lungs. The target creature repeats the save at the 
end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. 
After 10 minutes, it succeeds automatically.
